There's a famous quote from Steve Jobs about hiring talent that you've probably come across before:

> _It doesn't make sense to hire smart people and tell them what to do; we hire smart people so they can tell us what to do._

This quote speaks volumes about leadership styles. If you hire people only to dictate their every move, what you're really asking for is **obedience**, not expertise. But when you trust them to do their job, you're leveraging their **competence**; and competence always outperforms obedience.

# Do what I say

This leadership style has short legs—it won't take you far. If you're leading a team of five people but insist on making every decision yourself, what you really have is one brain and five pairs of hands. Sure, you gain more brute force to execute your ideas, but you're severely limiting the potential of your team.

The most powerful tool human beings have isn't their hands; it's their minds. When leaders operate with a 'do what I say' mindset, they waste a massive amount of human potential.

# Do your job

The real key to leadership is getting five brains thinking toward a shared goal, not just five hands executing orders. When a team's vision is aligned, that's when its full potential is unlocked.

Of course, this approach requires leaders to _let go of control_; something that isn't always easy. But trusting your team to perform at their best is the only way to build a truly effective and innovative organization.

# Needing to Be Told What to Do

Some team members are uncomfortable with autonomy. They prefer clear, step-by-step instructions and wait for permission rather than taking initiative. While structure is important, a team made up of passive followers can be just as ineffective as an overly controlling leader.

Great teams are made up of individuals who don't just execute tasks but actively contribute ideas, solve problems, and push things forward without waiting to be told. The best employees don't just do what they're asked—they think about what needs to be done and take action.

# Take over

Anyone can follow instructions. But true impact comes from those who don't just do what they're told; they do what needs to be done.
